'''Allen Neff''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ertegas/Legends|Ertegas]] who moved to [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] at the age of six, joining the [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Wing Guard]] that served the planet's [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]. Prior to the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[occupation of Bespin]] that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], Neff was among the Bespin Wing Guard [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] accompanying Cloud City's [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], in greeting the passengers of the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]&mdash;the Empire's intended target&mdash;as the [[Light freighter/Legends|vessel]] landed on Cloud City's [[Platform 327/Legends|Platform 327]].

==Biography==
[[File:Lando_Wing_Guards.png|thumb|300px|Lando Calrissian and his Bespin Wing Guard escorts greet Han Solo on Platform 327.]]
Born by [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]],<ref name="3 BBY" /> the [[Human/Legends|Human]]<ref name="ESB" /> [[Gender/Legends|male]]<ref name="FB" /> Allen Neff hailed from<ref name="SWI" /> the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Ertegas/Legends|Ertegas]]. He had a sister named [[Atril Neff|Atril]] and, at the age of six, left his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and moved to<ref name="SWI" /> the planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]].<ref name="SWI" /> Allen eventually followed his sister in joining the [[Bespin Wing Guard/Legends|Bespin Wing Guard]],<ref name="SWI" /> the main [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|security force]] of the planet's [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]].<ref name="Wing Guard DB">{{DB|organization|bespinwingguard|Wing Guard}}</ref>

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] [[Occupation of Bespin|occupied]] Bespin with the intent to capture the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="SWI" /> When the ''Millennium Falcon'' landed on Cloud City's [[Platform 327/Legends|Platform 327]], Neff was among the Wing Guard [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] accompanying the [[City/Legends|city's]] [[Baron Administrator/Legends|Baron Administrator]], [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and his chief [[Administrator/Legends|administrative]] [[Aide/Legends|aide]], [[Lobot/Legends|Lobot]], in greeting the [[Light freighter/Legends|freighter's]] [[Heroes of Yavin/Legends|occupants]]. Upon Lobot's command, Neff and the other Wing Guard left the Baron Administrator and his aide alone with the ''Falcon''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|captain]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], and his passengers, none of whom knew that Calrissian was in truth leading them into a trap set by the Empire.<ref name="ESB" />

==Personality and traits==
Allen Neff was light-skinned.<ref name="ESB" />

==Equipment==
During his service in the Bespin Wing Guard, Neff wore the standard [[Clothing/Legends|uniform]] of the organization.<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Elstree_Studios.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Elstree Studios, in which Allen Neff's actor was filmed on stage 2 between April 5 and 12, 1979]]
Allen Neff was created for the 1980 [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']],<ref name="ESB" /> released on [[May 21]] of that year.<ref name="Empire Turns 40">{{ThisWeek|6UccH037VQ0|The Empire Strikes Back Turns 40, Queen's Peril Gets a Voice, and More!|sw_url=video/the-empire-strikes-back-turns-40-queen-s-peril-gets-a-voice-and-more}}</ref> Prior to the film's release, he first appeared simultaneously in [[Shep Steneman]]'s ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''<ref name="ESB storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> and the film's [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]], written by [[Donald F. Glut]].<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> Both of the publications were released on [[April 12]] of the same year.<ref name="Amazon-RandomHouse">{{Amazon|url=Empire-Strikes-Back-Storybook/dp/0394844149|text=The Empire Strikes Back Storybook}}</ref><ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Neff's scene was filmed between [[April 5]] and April 12, [[1979]] on stage 2 of [[Elstree Studios]].<ref name="Making Of TESB">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

On [[March 11]], [[2014]],<ref name="Titan">{{TitanMagazines|url=t/star-wars-insider/us/148|text=Star Wars Insider Issue #148}}</ref> Neff was first named by the article "[[Rogues Gallery (department)|Rogues Gallery: The Cloud City Wing Guards]]," published in the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 148|148th issue]]. [[Kevin Beentjes]], [[Sander de Lange]], and [[Tim Veekhoven]], who wrote the article,<ref name="SWI" /> stated that nearly all of the Wing Guard members described were "good guys" who opposed the corruption that was prevalent under the leadership of Cloud City's previous Baron Administrator, [[Dominic Raynor]]&mdash;with the exception of the ones who had been previously established to have been corrupt.<ref name="FB" />
